newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Upside for June U.S. T-bonds seen limited.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Upside for June U.S. T-bonds seen limited.

text.p: June U.S. Treasury bond futures are at a critical juncture, but even if they are able to shake off recent woes, their upside will be limited, technical analysts said Wednesday.
"The focus right now technically is the 107-17/32 to 20/32 area," said Tim Ransford, a technical analyst at Dean Witter Reynolds in Chicago.
June bonds were up 02/32 at 107-17/32 in afternoon trade.
"Price action right here is going to be the difference between a huge drive up toward 110 or the market collapsing through the lows that we set last July," he said.
On a weekly chart, the July 1996 low for June bonds was 105-29/32.
Stewart Taylor, head of Taylor Consulting, said the trend is down and any rallies are likely to be limited.

"The recovery over the last couple of days is very nice and the market is very oversold," he said. "Typically you can expect an oversold condition and strong support to produce at least some sort of rally."
He said June bonds may have put in a near-term low at Tuesday's 106-25 session low and they could struggle back to the low to mid-109 area.
The 109-15/32 level represents a 38 percent retracement of the market's recent downmove, and its most recent high, set March 25, was 109-25/32, Taylor added.
"I would think any corrective rally would probably be confined to about that," he said. "So below 110."
Ransford said the more the market struggles at the 107-17/32 area, the more difficulty it will have breaking out to the upside.
"What's working for it at this stage is that near term, I really like the formation off the 106-25/32 low," he said. "That split two key reversal points.
"I think you could make a case that the very strong reaction" off 106-25 is solid, he said, adding that the key now is the 107-17/32 region.
"It's going to be the difference between whether this is just a garbage bounce off that low or really the beginning of something new," he said.
Taylor said a decline in open interest over the last couple of weeks indicated long positions being liquidated, which also helped set up a rally.
But he said the rally would likely run into "active" short selling in that 109 zone, driving the market back down.
